generation.explanation: The Inscribed Angle Theorem says that an angle inscribed in a circle (∠ACB) is exactly half the central angle (∠AOB) that subtends the same arc AB. Drag the yellow point C around the circle: as long as C stays on the same arc, the inscribed angle never changes, because the arc it subtends (highlighted in orange) is unchanged. If you drag C past A or B onto the other arc, it subtends the opposite arc and the angle becomes supplementary (the two values add to 180°). You can also drag A or B to change the arc itself and watch the 2:1 relationship update live.
